summary: John Dowson was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Edwin Norris. He taught as a tutor at the East India Company College (~1855–1858) and served as Professor of Hindustani at University College London and Staff College, Camberley (1855–1877).

John E. Cort is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his BA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1974) and his AM at Harvard University (~1982–1984). He held a professorship at Denison University (~1992).

John F. Richards was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of New Hampshire (~1957–1961) and UC Berkeley (~1961–1970). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1977) and Duke University (~1977–2007).

John Faithfull Fleet, an Indologist and historian, studied at University College London (~1865–1867). He served in the Indian Civil Service (1865–1897), the Bombay Civil Service (~1867–1897), and as Epigraphist for the Government of India (1883–1886).
John Fraser studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1903–1906). He held academic posts at the University of Aberdeen (~1906–1921) and the University of Oxford (~1921–1945).

Linguist and Central Asian specialist John Gombojab Hangin studied at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana universities. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Georgetown, UC Berkeley, Columbia, and Indiana University, where he became a full professor (1965–1989).
John H. Berthrong, a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religious studies, studied under graduate supervisor Alfonso Verdu. He held an appointment at Boston University, attested in 1996.
John Henry Hutton was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Worcester College, Oxford (~1904–1908), he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1909–1937).

John Henry Wright studied at Dartmouth and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He worked in linguistics and classical history, holding professorships at Ohio State (1873–1876), Dartmouth (1878–1886), Johns Hopkins (1886), and Harvard University (~1887–1908).

John Herbert Harington was an Indologist and historian. He served as secretary (1790) and president (1825–1828) of The Asiatic Society, and was an honorary professor at Fort William College around 1800.
John Hope studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1740–1750) and later held an academic post there from around 1761 to 1786.

John J. Holder, a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies, studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research post at the University of Oxford and served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at St. Norbert College (attested 2006, 2018).

John J. Makransky works in Buddhist studies, tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and under numerous traditional teachers, he held appointments at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Rangjung Yeshe Institute, and Boston College.

John James Jones was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Aberystwyth University (~1910–1915). He served as Deputy-Keeper of the Department of Printed Books at the National Library of Wales (~1943–1957).

John Jorgensen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology. He held research positions at the Australian National University and La Trobe University (attested 2019), and taught Japanese Studies at Griffith University.

John Kieschnick is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and history. He held a post at the University of Bristol (~2005–2011) before becoming Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation Professor of Buddhist Studies at Stanford University (~2011).

John Lane Bell is a philosopher who studied at the University of Oxford (~1963–1968). He held posts at the London School of Economics (~1968–1989), the University of Western Ontario (~1989), and the National University of Singapore.

John Lockwood Kipling, working in Indology and history, studied at Woodhouse Grove School. He taught at Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art (~1865–1875) and served as Principal of the National College of Arts and Curator of Lahore Museum (1875–1893).

John M. Koller is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena and Charles Alexander Moore. He served as a professor of philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, attested in 1988 and 1999.

John M. Rosenfield studied art history at SMU, UC Berkeley, Iowa, and Harvard under Benjamin Rowland. He was Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor at Harvard (1965–1991) and served as Curator at the Fogg Museum and Director of Harvard Art Museums.
